# Capacities Knowledge Graph Source

Source snapshot: `capacities.json`.

## Entities

Space, Object, Object Type, Property, Block, Tag, Collection, Query, Daily
Note, Task, Template, Image, Weblink, PDF, File, API Structure, API Token,
OAuth Connection.

## Features

Object Types, Properties, Block Editor, Tags, Collections, Queries, Search and
Command Palette, Daily Notes, Knowledge Graph, Templates, Task Management,
Task Actions, AI Assistant, AI Chat Connectors, Offline-First Work,
Synchronization, Media Management, Media Analysis, Import, Bulk Import,
Exports and Backups, Keyboard Shortcuts, Mobile, Tablet, REST API, MCP, and
Two-Factor Authentication.

## Workflows

Create an object; create a custom object type; build a network of notes; create
and reuse a query; create a recurring task; bulk import content; schedule a
full export; prepare a device for offline work; enable two-factor
authentication; use a personal API token; connect an MCP-capable client; and
configure a Readwise import.

## Graph Interpretation

Capacities models knowledge as connected objects with configurable types,
properties, blocks, tags, collections, and queries. This supports the generic
object foundation, but vendor-specific behavior remains reference material.

Capacities does not rely on folders or a traditional hierarchical note system; content revolves around objects and object types.

facts.text: Capacities does not rely on folders or a traditional hierarchical note system; content revolves around objects and object types.
Object types appear in the sidebar and can be customized with properties, layouts, and formatting.
Linking objects creates backlinks, and the graph view visualizes connections in the knowledge network.
The central calendar provides daily notes and date-related organization.
A suggested workflow is to inspect existing notes for natural groups, create useful object types, link objects with @, and use the daily note for capture.

The command palette is available with Cmd+K/Cmd+P on macOS and Ctrl+K/Ctrl+P on Windows.
Advanced inline object creation can use slash/plus syntax that includes the object type and new object name.

The AI Assistant is a paid AI feature intended to support writing, thinking, and organization within Capacities.

facts.text: The AI Assistant is a paid AI feature intended to support writing, thinking, and organization within Capacities.
The documentation describes selectable model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, and xAI, depending on current settings/availability.
AI-assisted workflows can operate on selected text or the active document, and results can be copied, used to replace selection, or appended to content.
AI functionality can use Capacities content/search context subject to the feature's documented privacy and availability constraints.

pages.summary: AI Chat Connectors are a Capacities Pro feature that connects external AI chat tools to a Capacities space using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

facts.text: AI Chat Connectors are a Capacities Pro feature that connects external AI chat tools to a Capacities space using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Connected assistants can search the space, read objects and properties, create pages/tasks/custom objects, update properties, append content, write to the daily note, and link to Capacities objects.
The documented MCP server URL is https://api.capacities.io/mcp.
Recurring tasks are not supported through AI Chat Connectors and should be created or edited in Capacities.

Documentation contains setup instructions for multiple MCP-capable clients including Claude Code, ClickUp, Gemini CLI/Enterprise/Workspace/Spark, Perplexity, Raycast, LM Studio, Cursor, VS Code, OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity, Android Studio, Langdock, Littlebird AI, Manus AI, Grok, Hermes Agent, and Dust.
Consumer Gemini web/mobile does not support custom MCP servers; the docs point to Gemini CLI and supported enterprise/workspace products for custom MCP use.
Active AI Chat Connector connections are managed under Settings > AI Assistant > AI Chat Connectors - Active Connections.

pages.summary: Task Management is a Capacities Pro feature and is opt-in.

facts.text: Task Management is a Capacities Pro feature and is opt-in.
Task management can be activated by creating the first Task object or adding Task from the basic object type section.
Tasks can be created from inline text with () + space or /task, the global task shortcut, the sidebar quick-add, task views, or the command palette.
The global task shortcut is Cmd+Shift+T on macOS and Ctrl+Shift+T on Windows.
Built-in task dashboard sections include Inbox, Today, Scheduled, Context, Tags, Open, Completed, and All.
Custom task dashboard sections can be created from queries.
A recurring task remains a single task object with a date property, recurrence rule, and occurrence history.
Recurring task presets include Daily, Weekly, Weekdays, Monthly, and Yearly, with a Custom option.
Completing a recurring occurrence logs it and advances the task to its next scheduled occurrence; if no future occurrence exists, the task becomes permanently done.
Overdue recurring tasks can offer advance-one or catch-up choices to move through missed occurrences.
Occurrences can be skipped or excused; excusing can preserve the streak without counting the occurrence as a completion.
Recurring-task statistics include current streak, best streak, total completions, completion rate, and for suitable recurrence patterns a heatmap.
The documentation labels the current task-management implementation as Version 1 and distinguishes roadmap ideas from current functionality.

pages.summary: Official Capacities documentation page: Task actions.
Queries are a Capacities Pro feature.

facts.text: Queries are a Capacities Pro feature.
Queries automatically gather and display content based on rules and can filter by properties, tags, content, or object types.
Query results update automatically as matching content changes.
Queries are objects, so they can be linked or embedded like other objects.
Object queries can include up to 10 object types and can additionally include/exclude collections, filter by tags/properties, sort, group, and limit results.
Saving a query creates a named query object that can be referenced elsewhere and can automatically appear as an object-dashboard section.
Search queries can save an extended-search configuration; extended search is opened with Cmd+Shift+P on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows.
Variable queries can refer to properties of the object in which the query is embedded, enabling context-aware reusable queries.

The integrations index documents first-party or officially supported connections including calendar integrations, Readwise, WhatsApp, Telegram, Email, task-manager actions, Kindle, Raycast, and Web Highlights.

facts.text: The integrations index documents first-party or officially supported connections including calendar integrations, Readwise, WhatsApp, Telegram, Email, task-manager actions, Kindle, Raycast, and Web Highlights.
Community integrations are listed separately and are explicitly not part of the official Capacities product, so their operation is not guaranteed by Capacities.

pages.summary: Capacities provides basic object types such as Page, Tag, Image, Weblink, Audio, PDF, File, Tweet, AI Chat, Query, Table, Daily Note, and Task, while also allowing custom object types.

facts.text: Capacities provides basic object types such as Page, Tag, Image, Weblink, Audio, PDF, File, Tweet, AI Chat, Query, Table, Daily Note, and Task, while also allowing custom object types.
Custom object types can be configured with properties, page layouts, dashboard behavior, card appearance, and default link views.
Object type dashboards can expose sections such as recently opened, untagged, without collection, without backlinks, collections, and an all-objects view.
Queries can be pinned as dashboard sections for supported paid functionality.

pages.summary: Block content is stored as a property of an object; media objects expose their notes through block content.

facts.text: Block content is stored as a property of an object; media objects expose their notes through block content.
Documented block types include rich text, code, mathematical/TeX content, tables, multi-column layouts, and embedded/transcluded content.
Blocks can be inserted through slash or plus commands and can be selected, moved, duplicated, styled, grouped, or transformed.

pages.summary: A property has a name, can have an icon and description, and has a property type.

facts.text: A property has a name, can have an icon and description, and has a property type.
Default properties are system-defined; the title property is especially important for identification and search.
Aliases can provide alternative names for objects.
Object-select properties create typed links to objects and can be configured for one or multiple values; relationships can support two-way linking.
Properties of basic object types have restrictions compared with custom object types and are not freely redefinable.

pages.summary: Capacities organization includes objects, object types, properties, labels, object-select properties, tags, queries, and collections.

facts.text: Capacities organization includes objects, object types, properties, labels, object-select properties, tags, queries, and collections.
Tags can organize content across object types and can also be applied to blocks.
Labels are useful for classifying objects within an object type.
Queries are rule-based, automatically updating views.
Collections are manually curated and belong to one object type.

pages.summary: Bulk Import is available through Settings > Import Content and includes a review/mapping flow before creating content.

facts.text: Bulk Import is available through Settings > Import Content and includes a review/mapping flow before creating content.
Bulk import can map imported data to object types and properties rather than blindly creating unstructured pages.
The desktop application should remain open while the bulk import is processing.
Imported document links can be resolved during import, but fragment-style file links such as PDF page fragments may not preserve the fragment semantics.

pages.summary: Exports are designed to be both human-readable and machine-readable.

facts.text: Exports are designed to be both human-readable and machine-readable.
Properties are transformed to front matter, collections to CSV files, media to separate human-readable folders, and links to local links so exported relationships remain portable.
Automated full exports can be scheduled from Settings > Full Export > Automated Full Export > Add Schedule by choosing spaces, a filesystem location, schedule, and options.
A single object can be exported from its three-dot menu as PDF, Markdown, Microsoft Word, or LaTeX; media can be downloaded as files.
Queries, tags, collections, and all objects of a type can be exported to CSV; selected objects can also be exported from supported views.

Capacities describes itself as offline-first: after login it downloads notes to the device, stores edits locally, and synchronizes changes when connectivity returns.

facts.text: Capacities describes itself as offline-first: after login it downloads notes to the device, stores edits locally, and synchronizes changes when connectivity returns.
Offline readiness can be checked under Settings > Offline & Sync; a device is fully offline-ready only after notes have finished downloading.
Media download can be configured as Everything or Required only. Desktop/mobile apps default to downloading all media, while browser usage defaults to Required only.
On mobile, background media downloads are restricted to Wi-Fi to reduce battery and network usage.
When local and server note versions conflict, Capacities asks the user to keep either the local or remote version; the discarded version cannot be recovered through that conflict dialog.
Full-text search, extended search, search queries, AI features, many task actions, and server-backed settings are not available or fully functional offline.
Offline-first does not mean notes are stored as user-visible Markdown files; content is stored in Capacities' own application/database storage.
Logging out deletes the locally stored Capacities data from the device.
Local app/browser data is not documented as encrypted on the device.
Completely disabling synchronization to Capacities servers is not supported and is not planned.

pages.summary: Content synchronizes across devices while connected to the internet.

facts.text: Content synchronizes across devices while connected to the internet.
Documented synchronization states include Offline, Synchronizing, Server is offline, Sync Server is offline, Synchronization failed, and Updating failed.
Troubleshooting includes checking connectivity, the Capacities status page, restarting the app, and checking VPN/firewall restrictions.
When Capacities or its sync server is offline, documentation warns against logging out or resetting the app while unsynchronized data may exist.
If updating fails, the app can be rebooted from Settings > Account > Reboot.

pages.summary: Media is processed locally and synchronized through a background upload pipeline; media can remain available locally while offline.

facts.text: Media is processed locally and synchronized through a background upload pipeline; media can remain available locally while offline.
Per-file upload limit is 100 MB for Basic, Pro, and Believer.
Basic is documented with a 100 MB monthly media upload limit and a 5 GB general storage limit.
Pro and Believer are documented as having unlimited monthly media upload and unlimited general media storage.
If an upload is interrupted, it resumes when a stable connection returns; until uploaded, the media is only available on the originating device.
If upload fails and the device also lacks sufficient local storage, a critical upload error can cause the file to be removed on reload and become unrecoverable.
Local processing extracts relevant metadata and can generate previews; corrupt files or failed metadata processing can produce processing errors.

facts.text: Open settings: macOS `Cmd + ,`; Windows `Ctrl + ,`.
Add new content: macOS `Cmd + U`; Windows `Ctrl + U`.
Search this space: macOS `Cmd + P or Cmd + K`; Windows `Ctrl + P or Ctrl + K`.
Open extended search (Pro): macOS `Cmd + Shift + P`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + P`.
Toggle dark mode: macOS `Shift + Cmd + L`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + L`.
Toggle focus mode (Pro): macOS `Shift + Cmd + M`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + M`.
Toggle left sidebar: macOS `Shift + Cmd + Left`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + Left`.
Toggle page sidebar: macOS `Shift + Cmd + Right`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + Right`.
Close current tab: macOS `Cmd + W`; Windows `Ctrl + W`.
Undo: macOS `Cmd + Z`; Windows `Ctrl + Z`.
Markdown-at-block-start shortcuts include quote, toggle, bullet list, numbered list, alphabetical list, Roman list, to-do, icon, horizontal line, and headings.
Block editing shortcuts include cut, copy, copy as Markdown, paste, paste as plain text, indent/unindent, style operations, duplicate, delete, turn into object, and group/ungroup.
The complete in-app shortcut cheat sheet is accessible from the Shortcuts button at the bottom-left of the main window and is searchable.

pages.summary: Account and authentication settings are available through the app settings.

facts.text: Account and authentication settings are available through the app settings.
Capacities supports authenticator-app based two-factor authentication and generates 10 backup codes during setup.
Account deletion is initiated from Settings > Account > Account Deletion and is followed by an email confirmation flow.
The documentation states that the account, notes, media, and data are permanently deleted after the deletion waiting period.
Email address changes are available under Settings > Account > Change email.

Spaces can be deleted from Settings > Space Settings > Delete Space; deleted spaces are soft-deleted for 30 days and can be restored from Settings > Account > Deleted Spaces unless permanently deleted.

facts.text: A table block can be created with + table or / table and starts with a small grid that can be expanded.

Documented table limitations include no bullet points inside cells, no images inside tables, and no cell merging.

The current Capacities API is a REST API that provides programmatic access to a single Capacities space per access token.

facts.text: The current Capacities API is a REST API that provides programmatic access to a single Capacities space per access token.
The API can read and write objects, properties, block content, daily notes, and related workspace data.
The current API base URL is https://api.capacities.io.
Personal API tokens are created from Settings > Capacities API and are scoped to a single space.
Documented API scopes include api:read and api:write.

pages.summary: The Capacities API uses Bearer authentication.

facts.text: The Capacities API uses Bearer authentication.
Personal tokens are intended for a user's own scripts and integrations and are tied to a selected space.
Third-party integrations use OAuth Authorization Code with PKCE; the docs describe verified clients and no client secret for public clients.
OAuth scopes include api:read, api:write, and offline_access.
OAuth authorization must identify the resource as https://api.capacities.io.
OAuth access tokens are documented with a one-hour lifetime.
Refresh tokens rotate and are documented to expire after six months of inactivity.
OAuth revocation is available at POST /oauth/revoke and follows the documented OAuth revocation behavior.

pages.summary: The officially documented SDK is a TypeScript package named @capacities/api.

facts.text: The officially documented SDK is a TypeScript package named @capacities/api.
The SDK handles authentication headers, API version headers, typed responses, and OAuth refresh behavior; direct HTTP clients are also supported.
The OAuth client proactively refreshes near expiry, can retry a refresh after a 401, and coordinates concurrent refresh activity.
No other official language SDK is documented on the SDK page at the time of retrieval.

pages.summary: API versions are selected with the X-Capacities-Api-Version request header.

facts.text: API versions are selected with the X-Capacities-Api-Version request header.
If the version header is omitted, requests use the latest API version according to the documentation.
The docs recommend pinning an API version for predictable integrations.
The current-version field on the retrieved Versioning page did not expose a concrete version value in the parsed content.

pages.summary: Rate limits are applied per token, per endpoint, and per time window.

facts.text: Rate limits are applied per token, per endpoint, and per time window.
Rate-limit state is communicated through a RateLimit response header containing limit, remaining, and reset values.
Exceeding an endpoint rate limit returns HTTP 429; clients should wait for reset and use backoff.
The API documents an object-creation quota with a hard limit of 5,000 objects and automatic incremental increases of 100 objects per month after the threshold is reached.
Exceeding the documented creation quota returns HTTP 403 with objectCreationQuotaReached.

pages.summary: API errors use standard HTTP status classes and a stable JSON error shape with a code, message, and optional details.

facts.text: API errors use standard HTTP status classes and a stable JSON error shape with a code, message, and optional details.
Documented error codes use a cap_ prefix, such as cap_invalid_input.

Object types are represented as structures in the API; each object has a structureId.

facts.text: Object types are represented as structures in the API; each object has a structureId.
Structures are retrievable from the space and contain metadata such as ID, title/plural name, property definitions, labels, and collections where applicable.
Structure and object identifiers are documented as UUIDs.
Space uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootSpace`.
Object type uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootStructure`.
Collection uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootDatabase`.
Query uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootQuery`.
Page uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootPage`.
Image uses the documented built-in structure identifier `MediaImage`.
PDF uses the documented built-in structure identifier `MediaPDF`.
Audio uses the documented built-in structure identifier `MediaAudio`.
Weblink uses the documented built-in structure identifier `MediaWebResource`.
File uses the documented built-in structure identifier `MediaFile`.
Tweet uses the documented built-in structure identifier `MediaTweet`.
AI Chat uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootAIChat`.
Table uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootSimpleTable`.

chunks.title: Capacities Documentation
chunks.text: Capacities documentation teaches an object-centered approach in which ideas are organized as connected objects rather than files buried in folders.

chunks.title: Getting started
chunks.text: Capacities does not rely on folders or a traditional hierarchical note system; content revolves around objects and object types.

chunks.title: Getting started
chunks.text: Object types appear in the sidebar and can be customized with properties, layouts, and formatting.

chunks.title: Getting started
chunks.text: Linking objects creates backlinks, and the graph view visualizes connections in the knowledge network.

chunks.title: Getting started
chunks.text: The central calendar provides daily notes and date-related organization.

chunks.title: Getting started
chunks.text: A suggested workflow is to inspect existing notes for natural groups, create useful object types, link objects with @, and use the daily note for capture.

chunks.title: Creating new objects
chunks.text: Objects can be created through the global new-content action, the command palette, type-specific actions, and text commands.

chunks.title: Creating new objects
chunks.text: The global add-new-content shortcut is Cmd+U on macOS and Ctrl+U on Windows.

chunks.title: Creating new objects
chunks.text: The command palette is available with Cmd+K/Cmd+P on macOS and Ctrl+K/Ctrl+P on Windows.

chunks.title: Creating new objects
chunks.text: Advanced inline object creation can use slash/plus syntax that includes the object type and new object name.

chunks.title: AI Assistant
chunks.text: The AI Assistant is a paid AI feature intended to support writing, thinking, and organization within Capacities.

chunks.title: AI Assistant
chunks.text: The documentation describes selectable model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, and xAI, depending on current settings/availability.

chunks.title: AI Assistant
chunks.text: AI-assisted workflows can operate on selected text or the active document, and results can be copied, used to replace selection, or appended to content.

chunks.title: AI Assistant
chunks.text: AI functionality can use Capacities content/search context subject to the feature's documented privacy and availability constraints.

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: AI Chat Connectors are a Capacities Pro feature that connects external AI chat tools to a Capacities space using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: Connected assistants can search the space, read objects and properties, create pages/tasks/custom objects, update properties, append content, write to the daily note, and link to Capacities objects.

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: The documented MCP server URL is https://api.capacities.io/mcp.

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: Recurring tasks are not supported through AI Chat Connectors and should be created or edited in Capacities.

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: Documentation contains setup instructions for multiple MCP-capable clients including Claude Code, ClickUp, Gemini CLI/Enterprise/Workspace/Spark, Perplexity, Raycast, LM Studio, Cursor, VS Code, OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity, Android Studio, Langdock, Littlebird AI, Manus AI, Grok, Hermes Agent, and Dust.

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: Consumer Gemini web/mobile does not support custom MCP servers; the docs point to Gemini CLI and supported enterprise/workspace products for custom MCP use.

chunks.title: AI Chat Connectors
chunks.text: Active AI Chat Connector connections are managed under Settings > AI Assistant > AI Chat Connectors - Active Connections.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Task Management is a Capacities Pro feature and is opt-in.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Task management can be activated by creating the first Task object or adding Task from the basic object type section.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Tasks can be created from inline text with () + space or /task, the global task shortcut, the sidebar quick-add, task views, or the command palette.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: The global task shortcut is Cmd+Shift+T on macOS and Ctrl+Shift+T on Windows.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Built-in task dashboard sections include Inbox, Today, Scheduled, Context, Tags, Open, Completed, and All.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Custom task dashboard sections can be created from queries.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: A recurring task remains a single task object with a date property, recurrence rule, and occurrence history.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Recurring task presets include Daily, Weekly, Weekdays, Monthly, and Yearly, with a Custom option.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Completing a recurring occurrence logs it and advances the task to its next scheduled occurrence; if no future occurrence exists, the task becomes permanently done.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Overdue recurring tasks can offer advance-one or catch-up choices to move through missed occurrences.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Occurrences can be skipped or excused; excusing can preserve the streak without counting the occurrence as a completion.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: Recurring-task statistics include current streak, best streak, total completions, completion rate, and for suitable recurrence patterns a heatmap.

chunks.title: Task Management
chunks.text: The documentation labels the current task-management implementation as Version 1 and distinguishes roadmap ideas from current functionality.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Queries are a Capacities Pro feature.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Queries automatically gather and display content based on rules and can filter by properties, tags, content, or object types.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Query results update automatically as matching content changes.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Queries are objects, so they can be linked or embedded like other objects.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Object queries can include up to 10 object types and can additionally include/exclude collections, filter by tags/properties, sort, group, and limit results.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Saving a query creates a named query object that can be referenced elsewhere and can automatically appear as an object-dashboard section.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Search queries can save an extended-search configuration; extended search is opened with Cmd+Shift+P on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows.

chunks.title: Queries
chunks.text: Variable queries can refer to properties of the object in which the query is embedded, enabling context-aware reusable queries.

chunks.title: Integrations
chunks.text: The integrations index documents first-party or officially supported connections including calendar integrations, Readwise, WhatsApp, Telegram, Email, task-manager actions, Kindle, Raycast, and Web Highlights.

chunks.title: Integrations
chunks.text: Community integrations are listed separately and are explicitly not part of the official Capacities product, so their operation is not guaranteed by Capacities.

chunks.title: Object types
chunks.text: Capacities provides basic object types such as Page, Tag, Image, Weblink, Audio, PDF, File, Tweet, AI Chat, Query, Table, Daily Note, and Task, while also allowing custom object types.

chunks.title: Object types
chunks.text: Custom object types can be configured with properties, page layouts, dashboard behavior, card appearance, and default link views.

chunks.title: Object types
chunks.text: Object type dashboards can expose sections such as recently opened, untagged, without collection, without backlinks, collections, and an all-objects view.

chunks.title: Object types
chunks.text: Queries can be pinned as dashboard sections for supported paid functionality.

chunks.title: Blocks
chunks.text: Block content is stored as a property of an object; media objects expose their notes through block content.

chunks.title: Blocks
chunks.text: Documented block types include rich text, code, mathematical/TeX content, tables, multi-column layouts, and embedded/transcluded content.

chunks.title: Blocks
chunks.text: Blocks can be inserted through slash or plus commands and can be selected, moved, duplicated, styled, grouped, or transformed.

chunks.title: Properties
chunks.text: A property has a name, can have an icon and description, and has a property type.

chunks.title: Properties
chunks.text: Default properties are system-defined; the title property is especially important for identification and search.

chunks.title: Properties
chunks.text: Aliases can provide alternative names for objects.

chunks.title: Properties
chunks.text: Object-select properties create typed links to objects and can be configured for one or multiple values; relationships can support two-way linking.

chunks.title: Properties
chunks.text: Properties of basic object types have restrictions compared with custom object types and are not freely redefinable.

chunks.title: Organizational structures
chunks.text: Capacities organization includes objects, object types, properties, labels, object-select properties, tags, queries, and collections.

chunks.title: Organizational structures
chunks.text: Tags can organize content across object types and can also be applied to blocks.

chunks.title: Organizational structures
chunks.text: Labels are useful for classifying objects within an object type.

chunks.title: Organizational structures
chunks.text: Queries are rule-based, automatically updating views.

chunks.title: Organizational structures
chunks.text: Collections are manually curated and belong to one object type.

chunks.title: Import
chunks.text: Single-file import supports documented text/document formats including Markdown, Microsoft Word, LaTeX, plain text, and HTML.

chunks.title: Import
chunks.text: The command palette can import a limited batch of images, files, PDFs, or text from the clipboard.

chunks.title: Bulk Import
chunks.text: Bulk Import is available through Settings > Import Content and includes a review/mapping flow before creating content.

chunks.title: Bulk Import
chunks.text: Bulk import can map imported data to object types and properties rather than blindly creating unstructured pages.

chunks.title: Bulk Import
chunks.text: The desktop application should remain open while the bulk import is processing.

chunks.title: Bulk Import
chunks.text: Imported document links can be resolved during import, but fragment-style file links such as PDF page fragments may not preserve the fragment semantics.

chunks.title: Exports and Backups
chunks.text: Exports are designed to be both human-readable and machine-readable.

chunks.title: Exports and Backups
chunks.text: Properties are transformed to front matter, collections to CSV files, media to separate human-readable folders, and links to local links so exported relationships remain portable.

chunks.title: Exports and Backups
chunks.text: Automated full exports can be scheduled from Settings > Full Export > Automated Full Export > Add Schedule by choosing spaces, a filesystem location, schedule, and options.

chunks.title: Exports and Backups
chunks.text: A single object can be exported from its three-dot menu as PDF, Markdown, Microsoft Word, or LaTeX; media can be downloaded as files.

chunks.title: Exports and Backups
chunks.text: Queries, tags, collections, and all objects of a type can be exported to CSV; selected objects can also be exported from supported views.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Capacities describes itself as offline-first: after login it downloads notes to the device, stores edits locally, and synchronizes changes when connectivity returns.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Offline readiness can be checked under Settings > Offline & Sync; a device is fully offline-ready only after notes have finished downloading.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Media download can be configured as Everything or Required only. Desktop/mobile apps default to downloading all media, while browser usage defaults to Required only.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: On mobile, background media downloads are restricted to Wi-Fi to reduce battery and network usage.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: When local and server note versions conflict, Capacities asks the user to keep either the local or remote version; the discarded version cannot be recovered through that conflict dialog.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Full-text search, extended search, search queries, AI features, many task actions, and server-backed settings are not available or fully functional offline.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Offline-first does not mean notes are stored as user-visible Markdown files; content is stored in Capacities' own application/database storage.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Logging out deletes the locally stored Capacities data from the device.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Local app/browser data is not documented as encrypted on the device.

chunks.title: Offline Support
chunks.text: Completely disabling synchronization to Capacities servers is not supported and is not planned.

chunks.title: Synchronization Status
chunks.text: Content synchronizes across devices while connected to the internet.

chunks.title: Synchronization Status
chunks.text: Documented synchronization states include Offline, Synchronizing, Server is offline, Sync Server is offline, Synchronization failed, and Updating failed.

chunks.title: Synchronization Status
chunks.text: Troubleshooting includes checking connectivity, the Capacities status page, restarting the app, and checking VPN/firewall restrictions.

chunks.title: Synchronization Status
chunks.text: When Capacities or its sync server is offline, documentation warns against logging out or resetting the app while unsynchronized data may exist.

chunks.title: Synchronization Status
chunks.text: If updating fails, the app can be rebooted from Settings > Account > Reboot.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: Media is processed locally and synchronized through a background upload pipeline; media can remain available locally while offline.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: Per-file upload limit is 100 MB for Basic, Pro, and Believer.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: Basic is documented with a 100 MB monthly media upload limit and a 5 GB general storage limit.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: Pro and Believer are documented as having unlimited monthly media upload and unlimited general media storage.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: If an upload is interrupted, it resumes when a stable connection returns; until uploaded, the media is only available on the originating device.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: If upload fails and the device also lacks sufficient local storage, a critical upload error can cause the file to be removed on reload and become unrecoverable.

chunks.title: Media Upload
chunks.text: Local processing extracts relevant metadata and can generate previews; corrupt files or failed metadata processing can produce processing errors.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Open settings: macOS `Cmd + ,`; Windows `Ctrl + ,`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Add new content: macOS `Cmd + U`; Windows `Ctrl + U`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Search this space: macOS `Cmd + P or Cmd + K`; Windows `Ctrl + P or Ctrl + K`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Open extended search (Pro): macOS `Cmd + Shift + P`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + P`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Toggle dark mode: macOS `Shift + Cmd + L`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + L`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Toggle focus mode (Pro): macOS `Shift + Cmd + M`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + M`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Toggle left sidebar: macOS `Shift + Cmd + Left`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + Left`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Toggle page sidebar: macOS `Shift + Cmd + Right`; Windows `Ctrl + Shift + Right`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Close current tab: macOS `Cmd + W`; Windows `Ctrl + W`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Undo: macOS `Cmd + Z`; Windows `Ctrl + Z`.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Markdown-at-block-start shortcuts include quote, toggle, bullet list, numbered list, alphabetical list, Roman list, to-do, icon, horizontal line, and headings.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: Block editing shortcuts include cut, copy, copy as Markdown, paste, paste as plain text, indent/unindent, style operations, duplicate, delete, turn into object, and group/ungroup.

chunks.title: Shortcuts
chunks.text: The complete in-app shortcut cheat sheet is accessible from the Shortcuts button at the bottom-left of the main window and is searchable.

chunks.title: Account & Authentication
chunks.text: Account and authentication settings are available through the app settings.

chunks.title: Account & Authentication
chunks.text: Capacities supports authenticator-app based two-factor authentication and generates 10 backup codes during setup.

chunks.title: Account & Authentication
chunks.text: Account deletion is initiated from Settings > Account > Account Deletion and is followed by an email confirmation flow.

chunks.title: Account & Authentication
chunks.text: The documentation states that the account, notes, media, and data are permanently deleted after the deletion waiting period.

chunks.title: Account & Authentication
chunks.text: Email address changes are available under Settings > Account > Change email.

chunks.title: Account & Authentication
chunks.text: Spaces can be deleted from Settings > Space Settings > Delete Space; deleted spaces are soft-deleted for 30 days and can be restored from Settings > Account > Deleted Spaces unless permanently deleted.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A first-class unit of knowledge in Capacities.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A structure/category defining what kind of object something is.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: Structured metadata attached to an object.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A manually curated group of objects within an object type.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A cross-object organizational mechanism.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A dynamic rule-based view that updates as matching content changes.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A reverse link showing where an object is referenced.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: A content unit within an object's block content.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text: Reusable structure/content for creating objects.

chunks.title: Tables
chunks.text: A table block can be created with + table or / table and starts with a small grid that can be expanded.

chunks.title: Tables
chunks.text: Table editing supports keyboard actions for inserting and moving rows and columns.

chunks.title: Tables
chunks.text: Tables can be exported as CSV and a table can be turned into an object.

chunks.title: Tables
chunks.text: Paid tiers document table formulas/functions including ABS, AVG, CEIL, COUNT, E, FLOOR, LOG, MAX, MEDIAN, MIN, PHI, PI, PRODUCT, RAND, ROUND, SIGN, SQRT, SUM, and TAU.

chunks.title: Tables
chunks.text: Documented table limitations include no bullet points inside cells, no images inside tables, and no cell merging.

chunks.title: Images
chunks.text: Images are first-class objects with structured metadata such as title, tags, description/notes, source/URL information, category, and colors.

chunks.title: Images
chunks.text: Paid AI/media analysis can generate metadata such as a title, short description, OCR text, category, and a color palette.

chunks.title: Images
chunks.text: Uploaded images can be available offline, while externally linked image URLs may expire and are not equivalent to locally synchronized media.

chunks.title: Images
chunks.text: Direct image attachment to the AI chat for OCR is not documented as supported on this page.

chunks.title: Weblinks
chunks.text: Weblink objects can store title, tags, description/notes, URL, category, topic, and keywords.

chunks.title: Weblinks
chunks.text: Weblinks can expose Browser, Reader, and Summary-oriented experiences where available.

chunks.title: Weblinks
chunks.text: Analyzed Reader content can be stored for offline use, while the live Browser view requires an internet connection.

chunks.title: Weblinks
chunks.text: Reader extraction may not always contain the full source article.

chunks.title: PDFs
chunks.text: PDFs can be uploaded, viewed, linked, and embedded as PDF objects.

chunks.title: PDFs
chunks.text: Native PDF annotation/highlighting is not documented as available.

chunks.title: PDFs
chunks.text: The built-in PDF object type does not provide the same custom-property freedom as a user-defined custom object type.

chunks.title: Files
chunks.text: Generic file objects can store arbitrary files up to the documented per-file media limit, with tags and notes.

chunks.title: Files
chunks.text: Generic file content is not edited directly inside Capacities; viewing may require downloading/opening the file externally.

chunks.title: Capacities on Mobile
chunks.text: The mobile app is positioned as a companion to desktop for searching, uploading, and taking notes on the go.

chunks.title: Capacities on Mobile
chunks.text: The mobile app is available for iOS and Android.

chunks.title: Capacities on Mobile
chunks.text: Primary bottom navigation includes Space overview, Calendar & Daily Note, Quick Action Palette, Search, and optionally AI Chat when AI is enabled.

chunks.title: Capacities on Mobile
chunks.text: The mobile space overview includes the space switcher, dark mode, settings, recent objects, open mobile tabs, pinned objects, and object types.

chunks.title: Capacities on Mobile
chunks.text: A right-side mobile sidebar provides quick access to search and recently opened items.

chunks.title: Capacities on Tablets
chunks.text: The tablet app combines desktop and mobile interaction patterns and is available for iPadOS and Android.

chunks.title: Capacities on Tablets
chunks.text: Documented tablet support includes creating/changing object types, properties, queries, data views, block references, extended/advanced search, command-bar functionality, bulk actions, templates, link views, and offline loading.

chunks.title: Capacities on Tablets
chunks.text: Documented tablet gaps include tabs, split screen, some keyboard shortcuts, swipe actions, and graph view.

chunks.title: Capacities on Tablets
chunks.text: Tablet supports full-text editing, property editing, object linking, and command access with @ and + similar to desktop.

chunks.title: Readwise
chunks.text: Readwise integration is a Capacities Pro feature for selectively importing Readwise documents and highlights.

chunks.title: Readwise
chunks.text: Readwise synchronization is one-way into Capacities.

chunks.title: Readwise
chunks.text: Automatic import of all newly processed Readwise content is constrained to one Capacities space.

chunks.title: Readwise
chunks.text: Readwise tags can be ignored, matched to existing tags, or imported depending on mapping choices.

chunks.title: Readwise
chunks.text: New highlights are processed periodically; upstream source timing can differ before Readwise itself exposes the content.

chunks.title: Readwise
chunks.text: The integration does not automatically bulk import the entire historical Readwise library; historical items can be selected/imported deliberately.

chunks.title: WhatsApp
chunks.text: The WhatsApp integration can send formatted messages, images, files, voice messages, and links into a Capacities daily note.

chunks.title: WhatsApp
chunks.text: Hashtag syntax can create or match tags, subject to tag-name restrictions.

chunks.title: WhatsApp
chunks.text: Documented object creation/linking syntax can target object types and titles from WhatsApp messages.

chunks.title: WhatsApp
chunks.text: A standalone web link can become a Weblink object.

chunks.title: WhatsApp
chunks.text: A numeric prefix can target another space when multiple spaces are available.

chunks.title: Unable to login
chunks.text: Login troubleshooting includes waiting after repeated attempts, changing network/device/browser, enabling JavaScript, trying private browsing, clearing browser data, disabling interfering extensions, and checking corporate/VPN restrictions.

chunks.title: Unable to login
chunks.text: Cloudflare Turnstile is part of the login protection flow and corporate/network filtering can interfere with it.

chunks.title: Email not verified
chunks.text: An email address must be verified before login; users should check inbox/spam and contact support if verification links fail or expire.

chunks.title: Login with Google
chunks.text: The documentation states that Google single sign-on is not offered; login uses email and password.

chunks.title: Capacities at work / corporate network
chunks.text: For restricted work/corporate networks, documentation recommends allowing Capacities domains and relevant infrastructure domains; documented examples include *.capacities.io and *.cloudflare.com.

chunks.title: Capacities API Beta (Deprecated)
chunks.text: The legacy Capacities API Beta documentation is marked deprecated and states that the beta API will be discontinued on September 1, 2026.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text: The current Capacities API is a REST API that provides programmatic access to a single Capacities space per access token.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text: The API can read and write objects, properties, block content, daily notes, and related workspace data.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text: The current API base URL is https://api.capacities.io.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text: Personal API tokens are created from Settings > Capacities API and are scoped to a single space.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text: Documented API scopes include api:read and api:write.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: The Capacities API uses Bearer authentication.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: Personal tokens are intended for a user's own scripts and integrations and are tied to a selected space.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: Third-party integrations use OAuth Authorization Code with PKCE; the docs describe verified clients and no client secret for public clients.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: OAuth scopes include api:read, api:write, and offline_access.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: OAuth authorization must identify the resource as https://api.capacities.io.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: OAuth access tokens are documented with a one-hour lifetime.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: Refresh tokens rotate and are documented to expire after six months of inactivity.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text: OAuth revocation is available at POST /oauth/revoke and follows the documented OAuth revocation behavior.

chunks.title: SDKs
chunks.text: The officially documented SDK is a TypeScript package named @capacities/api.

chunks.title: SDKs
chunks.text: The SDK handles authentication headers, API version headers, typed responses, and OAuth refresh behavior; direct HTTP clients are also supported.

chunks.title: SDKs
chunks.text: The OAuth client proactively refreshes near expiry, can retry a refresh after a 401, and coordinates concurrent refresh activity.

chunks.title: SDKs
chunks.text: No other official language SDK is documented on the SDK page at the time of retrieval.

chunks.title: Versioning
chunks.text: API versions are selected with the X-Capacities-Api-Version request header.

chunks.title: Versioning
chunks.text: If the version header is omitted, requests use the latest API version according to the documentation.

chunks.title: Versioning
chunks.text: The docs recommend pinning an API version for predictable integrations.

chunks.title: Versioning
chunks.text: The current-version field on the retrieved Versioning page did not expose a concrete version value in the parsed content.

chunks.title: Rate limiting
chunks.text: Rate limits are applied per token, per endpoint, and per time window.

chunks.title: Rate limiting
chunks.text: Rate-limit state is communicated through a RateLimit response header containing limit, remaining, and reset values.

chunks.title: Rate limiting
chunks.text: Exceeding an endpoint rate limit returns HTTP 429; clients should wait for reset and use backoff.

chunks.title: Rate limiting
chunks.text: The API documents an object-creation quota with a hard limit of 5,000 objects and automatic incremental increases of 100 objects per month after the threshold is reached.

chunks.title: Rate limiting
chunks.text: Exceeding the documented creation quota returns HTTP 403 with objectCreationQuotaReached.

chunks.title: Errors
chunks.text: API errors use standard HTTP status classes and a stable JSON error shape with a code, message, and optional details.

chunks.title: Errors
chunks.text: Documented error codes use a cap_ prefix, such as cap_invalid_input.

chunks.title: Structures
chunks.text: Object types are represented as structures in the API; each object has a structureId.

chunks.title: Structures
chunks.text: Structures are retrievable from the space and contain metadata such as ID, title/plural name, property definitions, labels, and collections where applicable.

chunks.title: Structures
chunks.text: Structure and object identifiers are documented as UUIDs.

chunks.title: Structures
chunks.text: Space uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootSpace`.

chunks.title: Structures
chunks.text: Object type uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootStructure`.

chunks.title: Structures
chunks.text: Collection uses the documented built-in structure identifier `RootDatabase`.

chunks.title: Structures

Full-text search, extended search, and search queries do not work offline; title search via command palette remains available.
AI features require server access and do not work offline.
Completely disabling server synchronization is not supported and is not planned.
Native PDF highlighting/annotation is not documented as available.
Tables do not support bullet points, images, or merged cells.
Tablet does not support tabs, split screen, graph view, swipe actions, and some keyboard shortcuts.
Recurring tasks cannot be created/edited through AI Chat Connectors.

faq.question: What should I try if I cannot log in?
faq.answer_summary: Check Turnstile/network/browser conditions, JavaScript, VPN/firewall, browser data/extensions, and password recovery; contact support if unresolved.

faq.question: Do I need to verify my email?
faq.answer_summary: Yes. Email verification is required before login.

faq.question: Can I sign in with Google?
faq.answer_summary: The documentation states that Google SSO is not offered; use email and password.

faq.question: Can I completely disable server synchronization?
faq.answer_summary: No; the offline documentation says this is not possible and not planned.

faq.question: Is local app data encrypted on the device?
faq.answer_summary: The offline documentation says local app/browser storage is not encrypted on-device.

coverage.coverage_statement: This JSON registers the complete primary navigation taxonomy and a broad set of recursively discovered official documentation pages. Detailed semantic extraction is strongest for core product, offline/sync, media, tasks, queries, AI connectors, import/export, apps, integrations, account, and developer/API concepts. Pages marked discovered/indexed are preserved instead of being silently omitted; their full body was not fully extracted in this pass.

validation.notes: Validation applies to the generated knowledge-base schema. It does not claim that every sentence of every official page was fully mirrored; extraction depth is explicit per page.
